body:
I’ve been really impressed with the HP OmniBook X Flip 2-in-1 so far. The build quality feels premium, and the 360-degree hinge is smooth and sturdy, making it easy to switch between laptop, tablet, and tent modes depending on what I’m doing.

The touchscreen display is excellent — sharp, bright, and very responsive. Whether I’m working, browsing, watching videos, or using it in tablet mode, everything looks great. The flexibility of this 2-in-1 design is a big plus and genuinely useful, not just a gimmick.

Performance has been fast and reliable for everyday tasks and multitasking. Apps open quickly, and the system feels smooth overall. I also appreciate the AI features and Copilot integration, which add some nice productivity touches, especially for work and meetings.

Battery life has been solid for daily use, and fast charging is convenient when I need a quick boost. The keyboard and trackpad are comfortable and responsive, though it did take a little time to adjust.

Overall, this is a well-rounded, modern 2-in-1 laptop that feels thoughtfully designed. It’s a great option if you want versatility, strong performance, and a premium feel in one device. I’d definitely recommend it to students, professionals, or anyone looking for a flexible laptop that can do it all.

title: decent ...but could be better
body:
The all-metal build does feel very good and for under $400 open-box+excellent it's good value .. but some aspects highlighted by Ad-like sounding reviews need to be highlighted

1. the speakers are *not* located left/right of the keyboard; those are fake speaker grilles. The speakers are behind the touch rest and the sound comes out of 2 small slits facing the users - for usable sound the laptop will need to be placed on a hard surface (i.e. won't work if you're holding it on your lap or any non-hard surface). 

2. sound can be loud enough but still tinny. "spatial audio" is a gimmick when you have small speakers that don't even face the user. Sound quality (stereo separation, clarity, "fullness") is light years away from Asus Zephyrus G16, G14 + MBP 14 devices I own. It might be good enough for a Zoom conference but nowhere near enough for music listening or music watching - it torpedoes the "immersive-ness".

3. Integrated graphics do *not* come with dedicated 8GB. those are "up to 8GB of RAM" that come from the meager 16GB of total RAM available. 

4. Windows OS/x64 eats battery for breakfast; significantly higher standby battery drain than Windows/Arm for a Snapdragon Omni 5 16 that I own

title: One flaw keeps it from being great!
body:
Very good with a few very big issues. 

What you will love:

Flips to a tablet (includes kickstand mode for easily keeping it up right).

Pen support (unfortunately not included).

The GPU can run some decent games at playable frame rates.

The keyboard is honestly more comfortable to type on than I was expecting.

The screen is sharp with a 16:10 aspect ratio. 

Hard Drive is replaceable.

The build quality is top notch and rivals the MacBook Air.

The Battery Life will go a good 12 hours in many situations.

What you likely won’t like. 

RAM is soldered on the chip and that means all you’re going to have is 16 Gigs.

The GPU shares the main RAM and dynamically allocates between 4 and 8 gig to the GPU.  That means your games could run out of RAM or VRAM.  

Even when using an external GPU, the computer wouldn’t release the minimal 4 Gigs that were allocated to the GPU and this was not something it allowed me to change for some bizarre reason.  

Would I recommend this?

If you’re just looking at this as an alternative to a MacBook Air and you want it to do similar things for less money?  Absolutely!  In many ways it is a better MacBook Air than the MacBook Air. 

If you want it as a part time gaming solution or for creating content, I would skip this and look for Omnibook X models that have either the Ryzen 7 AI 350 or the Intel Core Ultra 258V as that is the same as this with double the RAM.

title: Great all-around 2-in-1 laptop with modern AI feat
body:
I’ve been using the HP OmniBook X Flip (16", Intel Core Ultra 5, 16GB RAM) for a few weeks now, and overall I’m really impressed with what it offers — especially if you’re looking for a sleek, powerful 2-in-1 with some next-gen features.

What I love:

Big, bright 2K touchscreen is perfect for multitasking, watching videos, and even some sketching or note-taking with a stylus. The 16:10 aspect ratio gives extra room for work and school stuff.

Build quality feels premium — lightweight for a 16” laptop and the 360° hinge is solid. I use it in tablet and tent mode a lot for casual streaming.

The Intel Ultra 5 processor is snappy — everything from Chrome tabs to Office to Zoom runs smoothly. The 512GB SSD keeps it feeling fast.

AI features like Copilot+ are interesting. I haven’t used them a ton yet, but it’s nice knowing the hardware is ready for future updates.

Keyboard and trackpad are comfortable, and it has a surprisingly good selection of ports — no need to carry tons of dongles.

What to know:

Battery life is just okay. I get about 5–6 hours on average when using it for work or school. You’ll probably want to carry your charger.

Some preinstalled HP software runs in the background and eats up resources — I disabled a few things and performance got even better.

Tablet mode is cool, but at 16", it’s a little bulky to hold for long periods. Probably better on a desk than in your hands.

RAM isn’t upgradeable, so choose your config wisely.

Verdict:

If you want a well-rounded Windows laptop that also flips into a tablet and can handle everything from work to streaming to light creative tasks — this is a great choice. The AI stuff is still early days, but the laptop itself is solid and future-ready. I’d definitely recommend it to students, remote workers, and anyone who wants flexibility without sacrificing performance.
